articles.title: I tried Gen Z’s newest ways to find love. Here’s what I learned
articles.summary: Is Gen Z done with dating apps? These companies are betting on it. Gen Zers are trying viral matchmaking photo booths, in person speed dating and analog acqu...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Ask anyone, dating in 2026 is rough.

I'm 24, single, and living in a city with nearly 8.5 million people. Theoretically, there should be more potential for matches here than anywhere else.

And yet, in conversations with my 20-something friends, sources and dating experts alike, I keep hearing the same thing: dating apps, which once seemed to hold limitless possibilities, feel more like an online shopping cart of options where there's a paradox of choice. It's never been easier to connect, and yet, we're more isolated than ever.

Is it so crazy that I'd like to meet my person, well, in person?

As a growing portion of Gen Zers burn out on dating apps, a new crop of ventures and events are trying to bring back offline spontaneity, from matchmaking photobooths, to singles mixers and revivals of Victorian-era acquaintance cards.

So, for a month, I set out to follow Gen Z's search, scouring the city for a modern-day meet cute.

That's how I find myself at Baby's All Right, the institution of Brooklyn's indie music scene that was referenced in Lorde's single "What Was That." I last frequented the venue to watch The Dare perform, but the evening of Aug. 13, I'm here to cheer on those who'll go on stage to pitch a packed crowd on why they should date their friend.

"Who here is tired of dating online?" one of the "About my Friend" event organizers, Petro Anastos-Prastacos, shouts to cheers. "We're here to meet people IRL, not URL!"

A woman presents her former co-worker Becca, who planned a one-woman cabaret show for her birthday and is a "top 1% friend" who "never forgets to check in with you." There's Ariana from Florida, who almost exclusively shops for her groceries at Union Square Market but is also down for a slice of pizza any time. One friend, who affectionately describes her friend Sam, makes the case that "we're all sleeping on the short guys when we should be sleeping with them."

Roughly 2,500 people have attended the 22 events the group has thrown since Brit O'Brien and Anastos-Prastacos launched the group in January.

It's one of many creative events that have popped up to help people meet in-person. Eventbrite found a 117% increase in U.S. events using "meet cute" language in the first half of 2026, with attendance up 128% from the same period last year.

"The proliferation of dating apps and now AI optimizing the dating process has made romance very transactional," says Amy Chan , a dating coach and the author of " Unsingle: How to Date Smarter and Create Love that Lasts ," "The 'meet cute' is the antithesis of that. It injects magic and serendipity into the equation."

There are live comedy dating shows like UpDating and Where there's a Will There's a Way , the dating event series Met Through Friends , which hosts a plus one party where each guest must bring a single friend of the opposite sex, and groups like Hot and Social , a company that organizes in-person gatherings for people in their late 20s to 40s to meet.

There are other creative ways singles have taken matters into their own hands. Some have sported "I'm Single" hats and "Looking for my future husband" shirts with a QR code.

They're dating for dinner. And they're not alone

Alice Marks, 30, and Jonathan Gilmour, 29, were introduced at a March "About my Friend" event in Ridgewood after their friends pitched them on stage. They met on the steps of The Metropolitan Museum of Art for their first date a week later, and have now been dating for five months.

Both previously dabbled in dating apps and know plenty of people who met long-term connections that way — Marks' older sister met her partner on an app, and they now have two children together. But both say they felt "unsatisfied" with the experiences.

More than half of adults under 30 report having used dating apps like Tinder, Match, Bumble, and Hinge, according to 2023 data from Pew Research .

There's a lingering sense that it's somehow embarrassing to use these apps, and yet the possibility that prince charming might be hiding beneath a slate of bad matches and a few tasteless sex jokes keeps us from deleting them.

That algorithmic loop can be exhausting, and a Forbes Health survey found that 79% of Gen Zers report burnout from apps.

With horror stories and red flags amplified on social media, Chan says trust levels are also lower than ever.

And apps are responding — Tinder in March launched an events tab in select markets. In NYC, 66% of Gen Z users have engaged with the feature, according to Global Chief Marketing Officer Melissa Hobley. A wave of new apps like Cerca and Frnds of Frnds have popped up with the premise of connecting users through mutual friends.

"For most of human history, you met people through friends, community, work, school, and there were social consequences if you behaved poorly," Chan says. "The apps removed that, and now it seems like the market demand is putting it back in."

Gen Z's dating style reflects a deeper trend of risk aversion — young people are also drinking less and having less sex . While those things can be positive, they're also indicators that some Gen Zers are socially isolated. Much of Gen Z missed out on pivotal years in the classroom or office during the pandemic, impacting their ability to socialize.

Evolving gender roles in the home and workplace, steep political polarization and the growing cost of dating have all reshaped the social norms around how people engage further.

"This generation never got to experience dating before app culture, doom scrolling and social media," says Chan . "They're not longing for something they lost, they're longing for an idea of something — something that must have been better than what their current reality is."

Chan says these in-person dating events are a "win win" situation. Even if people don't meet a romantic interest, they walk away with improved socialization skills, a new hobby or a new friend.

Matchmaking photobooths, acquaintance cards and 'I'm Single' merch

When 28-year-old Margot Lee got out of a long-term relationship in 2025 and found herself single for the first time in New York, she thought dating would happen organically. Her parents met at a beach town sharehouse through mutual friends, and she grew up watching "Sex and the City."

"People just aren't really mixing and mingling at bars anymore," Lee tells me. "Dating aside, if I'm just having a fun night with my friends, I think it's exponentially more fun when you meet new people and kind of like collect characters throughout the night, and I was just noticing that that wasn't happening."

Her brand No Particular Order on Valentine's Day of 2026 started selling Victorian-era inspired acquaintance cards , which they advertise as the "analog solution to dating." They were supposed to be a gag product, meant as a seasonal item, but they became the brand's best seller.

The cards were a hit with my friends when I brought them to a get together before a night out.

Later in the month, I went to Union Square to check out a viral matchmaking photo booth intended to set up singles. "Every great love story starts with a meet cute. Yours might start here," reads the homepage of the booth's online questionnaire.

Before I step inside, I answer questions on a sliding scale of one to seven about the importance of finances, religion and family in my life.

After tapping my card for $10 and posing for a series of photos, the photo strip comes out, but it isn't just mine. I also receive one from the person I've been matched with, bearing their first name only. Presumably, this cycle will repeat when a copy of my pictures is given to someone else.

I meet Sophia Degraye, 23, in line for the booth, who tells me she wishes older generations understood that dating today is "so complicated" between situationships and the ambiguity of modern relationships.

"I'd rather this than an online dating app," says Degraye of the photobooth. "A lot of my friends have found really happy relationships there, but I feel like this is a bit more organic."Degraye ends up paying for another photo strip, and this time, poses with a photo of her Instagram handle, hoping to make it easier for her match to track her down.

But the booth, run by @meetcutesnyc and matchmaking company Matchbox, feels more like a marketing experiment made with social media in mind. Advertisements around the booth direct passerbyers to @boothmaxxing , an account where users can post their missed connections.

By the end of the month, I'm thinking less about whether these experiments lead to relationships and more about the ways they've pushed my social skills and forced me out of my comfort zone.

It's a lesson I learned early on in the month.

On Aug. 12, I attend a West Side Highway event with Leg Day , an app designed to help gym-goers connect with their gym crushes in real time.

"Everyone wants to find their person on the WSH. For one night, they can," a Partiful invitation with more than 2,783 "yes" RSVPs advertises.

So I show up to the West Side Highway ready to connect, hoping my fellow runners will think my sweat from the August heat is just a sign of my athletic prowess. But when I arrive, the app has crashed, overloaded with viewers.

The Partiful comments quickly become a place for people to advertise their own startups and commiserate on their misfortune.

But something else special happens, too.

"Guys, I think we can just go to each other without the app too if we have to," one person comments. Another suggests everyone meets up at Pier 46.

When I get there and join a conversation with a group of girls, I'm surprised to hear they've only just met each other. We look out for each other as we walk to the bar, where the app's crashing has ironically become an easy conversation starter. Before the night ends, I even exchange numbers with one of my new friends.

Across each of these dating events, I find that people are genuinely excited to meet each other, and plenty have come alone solely looking for platonic connections. Despite the fear my generation has about rejection, it turns out most people are just as nervous as the rest of us.

We spend a lot of time trying to engineer the perfect way to meet someone. Perhaps we could all use a reminder that sometimes, the hardest part is simply being less afraid to put ourselves out there.

articles.title: ‘Dhartipakad’ from Bihar who contested 281 elections and won none dies at 96
articles.summary: Nagarmal Bajoria aka Dhartipakad, Bhagalpur social worker and famed “never-winning” election contestant, dies at 96; he fought 281 polls, including top posts.
articles.body: BHAGALPUR: Maverick social worker and indefatigable election contestant Nagarmal Bajoria, popularly known as Dhartipakad, died at the age of 96 in Bhagalpur on Thursday. A resident of Sujaganj main market, he will be cremated at Barari Ghat on Friday.Bajoria contested 281 elections but never won one. His famous line was: “I do not lose elections, but the people always do.”His electoral journey took him from municipal corporation polls to parliamentary elections in Patna and Delhi. He contested against political stalwarts, including Indira Gandhi, Rajiv Gandhi, Sanjay Gandhi, Atal Bihari Vajpayee and L K Advani.His first electoral contest was against then presidential candidate V V Giri in 1969. He later contested 18 times for the posts of President and Vice-President of India, with his last, 281st, election coming in 2019.Born in Lahore in undivided India, Bajoria migrated to Bhagalpur in the 1930s and established a business in the city’s main market. He also devoted himself to social work, arranging mass marriages for poor girls to promote simple, dowry-less weddings and helping install tube-wells at places where drinking water was needed.For Bajoria, elections were less about becoming an MP or MLA and more about drawing attention to social and national issues and encouraging voters to choose the best candidate.His grandson Gourav Bajoria said his grandfather was a committed social worker with immense love for the country. “Though electoral victory eluded him, his constant participation in the democratic process, courage to challenge the system and never-say-die attitude will live long in the memories of the people of Bhagalpur,” he said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: Saiba como cidade em SP entrou na rota de shows internacionais | G1
articles.standfirst: São José do Rio Preto (SP) recebe Maroon 5 no domingo (6). Em abril, a cidade foi palco de uma apresentação de Guns N' Roses. A dupla Zé Neto & Cristiano está por trás das negociações.
articles.summary: Com uma população estimada em 506.466 habitantes, São José do Rio Preto (SP) entrou na rota de shows internacionais em 2026.
articles.body:
Com uma população estimada em 506.466 habitantes, São José do Rio Preto (SP) entrou na rota de shows internacionais em 2026. Localizado próximo aos estados de Minas Gerais e Mato Grosso do Sul, o município recebeu Guns N' Roses em abril e será palco da estreia da turnê “Love is Like” do Maroon 5 no domingo (6).

Os propulsores desse cenário são os cantores Zé Neto & Cristiano . A dupla sertaneja possui uma produtora, a qual teve participação expressiva nos investimentos para viabilizar as atrações das duas bandas estrangeiras.

Zé Neto e Cristiano são nascidos em São José do Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: Thomaz Marostegan - Arquivo

Criados na zona rural de Ipiguá (SP), os sertanejos nasceram em São José do Rio Preto e residem no município até os dias atuais. Além da agenda de shows, as caminhadas na represa da cidade também fazem parte da rotina dos músicos e de suas famílias.

Ao acreditar no potencial econômico local, Zé Neto contou, em entrevista ao g1 , que ele e o parceiro de palco decidiram apostar nas atrações internacionais.

“Somos apaixonados por Rio Preto, sempre tentamos fazer de tudo o que está em nosso alcance para a melhoria da cidade. A principal motivação foi a população mesmo, pensar em trazer esses shows, que podem ser a realização de um sonho para muitas pessoas que não podem se locomover até outros locais para assistir, é incrível. Queremos proporcionar momentos únicos para os moradores daqui”, explica o sertanejo.

banda Maroon 5 — Foto: Maroon 5/ Facebook

A banda norte-americana Maroon 5 se apresentará no Recinto de Exposições Alberto Bertelli Lucatto. No domingo, o evento deverá reunir 25 mil pessoas em São José do Rio Preto, além de gerar uma movimentação econômica em torno de R$ 20 milhões.

O palco terá 50 metros de largura, 18 metros de altura e 20 metros de profundidade, além da passarela que permitirá maior flexibilidade aos artistas. A estrutura é composta por um “paredão” de LED de 28x12 metros e mais de 600 aparelhos de iluminação com tecnologia de ponta.

Questionado pela reportagem, o cantor Cristiano garantiu que a cidade tem potencial para receber os artistas americanos.

“A gente sabe que muita coisa tem que melhorar. Hoje, a gente não tem um estádio, uma arena pronta para esses shows, mas quem sabe um dia, de pouquinho a pouquinho. Acreditamos que Rio Preto pode ser o grande polo do interior para o entretenimento”, explica.

Banda Guns N’ Roses faz show inédito em São José do Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

No dia 7 de abril, foi a vez do Guns N' Roses se apresentar em solo rio-pretense. O show histórico teve duração de quase três horas e movimentou R$ 17,4 milhões. Com setlist de 24 músicas, o evento reuniu cerca de 30 mil pessoas no recinto de exposições.

Segundo Zé Neto, a produtora tem projetos de trazer mais atrações internacionais para o município.

São José do Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: Divulgação / Prefeitura de São José do Rio Preto

“A gente tem vontade de trazer mais shows como esses para a nossa cidade. O povo na internet está pedindo muita coisa. A gente tenta ouvir, mas tudo depende dos nossos parceiros, das negociações. Se tudo der certo, não vamos parar por aqui não”, garante.

Nomes como Shakira e Bon Jovi estão entre os mais pedidos pelo público nas redes sociais. Questionado, Cristiano esclareceu que, por enquanto, são apenas alguns desejos da população, mas que novas negociações poderão ocorrer a qualquer momento.

Montagem do palco para o show do Guns N'Roses no Recinto de Exposições em São José do Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

“Um show internacional move muito emprego e precisamos de muitas pessoas envolvidas para fazer tudo sair nos conformes. E fora do show, também é algo grandioso. No Guns N’ Roses, ficamos sabendo que a rede de hotelaria de Rio Preto ficou completamente esgotada. Pensa no quanto isso não gerou de emprego indireto e movimentou a cidade”, finaliza o segunda voz da dupla.

Adam Levine (à esquerda) e Axl Rose (à direita) — Foto: Arquivo / g1

articles.title: Churrasqueira de ferro fundido em varanda de apartamento: o que verificar | G1
articles.standfirst: Antes de comprar uma churrasqueira para a varanda do apartamento, veja o que o regimento do condomínio, a fumaça e o tipo de peça exigem
articles.summary: Antes de comprar uma churrasqueira para a varanda do apartamento, veja o que o regimento do condomínio, a fumaça e o tipo de peça exigem
articles.body:
A vontade de ter uma churrasqueira de ferro fundido na varanda do apartamento esbarra em três coisas que muita gente só descobre depois da compra: o regimento do condomínio, o controle da fumaça e o tamanho da peça no espaço disponível. Verificar esses pontos antes evita compra errada e briga com o vizinho.

Churrasqueiras de ferro fundido compactas: modelos que cabem em varanda de apartamento — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

Regimento do condomínio: confirme se churrasqueira a carvão é permitida; muitos só liberam elétrica ou a gás.

Fumaça: modelos a bafo ou com tampa reduzem a fumaça que incomoda os andares de cima.

Tamanho: meça a varanda e escolha peça compacta ou portátil que não bloqueie a circulação.

Piso e parede: proteja a superfície do calor; evite fixar sem autorização em área comum.

Por que o ferro fundido combina com varanda

A churrasqueira de ferro fundido compacta tem uma vantagem para apartamento: distribui o calor por igual e permite assar com menos brasa, o que significa menos fumaça. Os modelos portáteis e as versões porquinho, gaúcha e stylus ocupam pouco espaço e podem ser guardados quando não estão em uso — solução prática para varanda pequena.

Verifique o regimento antes de tudo: muitos condomínios só liberam churrasqueira a gás ou elétrica na varanda.

A escolha certa cabe no espaço e no regimento. As churrasqueiras de ferro fundido incluem modelos compactos e portáteis adequados a varanda.

Sediada em Divinópolis , no Centro-Oeste de Minas, a Panela de Ferro Fundido trabalha com churrasqueiras em ferro fundido. Os modelos estão no catálogo de churrasqueiras de ferro fundido , com entrega para todo o Brasil.

articles.title: Incêndio na Rodovia Luiz de Queiroz atinge carga em Americana | G1
articles.standfirst: Ocorrência foi registrada no km 128, na região do Jardim Glória. Ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.summary: O incêndio na Rodovia Luiz de Queiroz atingiu carga de livros e peças de bicicleta no km 128, em Americana, sem deixar feridos durante o combate às chamas.
articles.body:
Um incêndio atingiu a carga de um caminhão na manhã desta sexta-feira (4), na Rodovia Luiz de Queiroz (SP-304), em Americana (SP). O veículo transportava peças de bicicletas e livros.

A ocorrência foi registrada no km 128, na região do Jardim Glória. De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros, as equipes foram acionadas às 4h37.

Três viaturas foram enviadas ao local para combater as chamas. O trabalho foi encerrado às 7h20. Ninguém ficou ferido.

articles.title: Ilha misteriosa aparece e desaparece em lago no Canadá | G1
articles.standfirst: Num reservatório no norte do Canadá, uma ilha coberta de árvores e maior que um campo de futebol sumiu das imagens de satélite e reapareceu em outro lugar.
articles.summary: Num reservatório no norte do Canadá, uma ilha coberta de árvores e maior que um campo de futebol sumiu das imagens de satélite e reapareceu em outro lugar.
articles.body:
Ilha misteriosa aparece e desaparece em lago no Canadá — Foto: Rocky Avery/Facebook

No lago de Williston, no norte da Colúmbia Britânica, no Canadá, surgiu, desapareceu e depois voltou a aparecer uma enorme formação flutuante que, durante semanas, deixou os moradores intrigados, despertou o interesse de vários especialistas e acabou se transformando num pequeno mistério natural.

Trata-se de uma ilha flutuante coberta por árvores densas e aparentemente saudáveis, com uma área de quase um hectare, ou mais do que um campo de futebol. Não parece ser uma obra humana. Ninguém sabe ao certo de onde ela veio. E, durante semanas, nem sequer se sabia onde ela estava.

As primeiras imagens começaram a circular em agosto. Um navegador registrou a formação a partir da água, e o material acabou chegando às mãos de Rocky Avery, morador da região, que o compartilhou nas redes sociais. Em pouco tempo, as imagens atraíram enorme atenção. Avery afirmou à emissora canadense CBC que, em 40 anos vivendo no Canadá, nunca havia visto algo semelhante.

A cena parecia tão incomum que até mesmo a B.C. Hydro, empresa de energia responsável pela administração da barragem W.A.C. Bennett e do lago, que é um reservatório, duvidou inicialmente de sua autenticidade. Seu porta-voz, Bob Gammer, explicou à CBC que o crescimento dos vídeos gerados por inteligência artificial obriga a analisar com cautela qualquer imagem publicada na internet.

Os satélites confirmam e depois perdem a ilha

As dúvidas desapareceram com a ajuda dos satélites. Uma imagem de 21 de julho localizou a ilha cerca de 100 quilômetros a oeste da barragem. A B.C. Hydro estimou que ela media aproximadamente 70 por 140 metros, totalizando cerca de 9.800 metros quadrados, segundo dados divulgados pela CBC.

Ilha 'desaparece' no Canadá — Foto: Rocky Avery/Facebook

Pouco depois, tão repentinamente quanto surgiu, ela desapareceu. Em 5 de agosto, já não aparecia nas imagens de satélite e ninguém podia afirmar com certeza se havia afundado ou simplesmente alcançado uma área mais protegida próxima à margem.

O mistério foi resolvido no fim de agosto. A B.C. Hydro confirmou que a ilha havia encalhado na entrada norte do braço de Ospika, a cerca de 30 quilômetros de sua última localização conhecida, uma distância que chamou a atenção de alguns dos especialistas consultados.

O mistério despertou interesse até mesmo fora do Canadá. Segundo a CBC, Finlay Farquhar, um residente do Reino Unido ligado à área de engenharia de rádio, acompanhou os rastros da formação por conta própria e acabou identificando sua nova posição utilizando ferramentas públicas de imagens de satélite.

Esse deslocamento tem uma explicação provável. Segundo Gammer, ele se deveu não à correnteza, que nesse trecho do reservatório se move muito lentamente em direção à barragem, mas ao vento, capaz de empurrar uma massa desse tamanho por águas abertas.

A formação da ilha continua sendo uma das grandes incógnitas do caso. A principal hipótese está relacionada aos níveis excepcionais da água. Após um inverno com muita neve e um verão chuvoso, o reservatório de Williston atingiu sua capacidade máxima pela primeira vez em 14 anos, obrigando a B.C. Hydro a abrir os vertedouros em junho e julho.

Uma das possibilidades levantadas por Gammer é que o processo de formação da ilha tenha começado muito antes de alguém perceber. Restos de árvores e outros materiais teriam se acumulado gradualmente numa área protegida, criando ao longo do tempo uma base sobre a qual a vegetação pôde crescer. A elevação extraordinária do nível da água teria finalmente desprendido essa estrutura, deixando-a flutuar livremente.

As condições das margens também teriam favorecido o processo. O geólogo John Clague, da Universidade Simon Fraser, acrescenta que a erosão acumulada tornou alguns trechos das margens mais instáveis. Além disso, os fortes ventos da região são capazes de gerar ondas e afetar as árvores próximas à costa.

O fenômeno, aliás, não é tão excepcional para quem estuda esse tipo de formação. A pesquisadora da National Geographic Natalie Kramer Anderson, especializada em acúmulos de troncos e madeira, explica que grandes depósitos de madeira podem permanecer estáveis por décadas e acabar servindo de base para o crescimento de nova vegetação.

A ecóloga marinha Rebecca Helm, da Universidade de Georgetown, insere o fenômeno num contexto mais amplo. Na avaliação dela, esse tipo de ilha provavelmente era mais comum no passado, antes que a atividade humana modificasse muitos dos processos naturais que favoreciam sua formação.

"Esta ilha parece mais um velho fantasma do que um novo fenômeno, algo que os seres humanos costumavam ver com muito mais frequência", afirmou Helm à National Geographic.

Existem outros exemplos semelhantes em várias regiões do mundo. Em Wisconsin, nos Estados Unidos, a chamada Forty Acre Bog muda de posição periodicamente e precisa ser deslocada todos os anos para evitar que derive em direção a uma ponte. No Lago Vitória, na África, formações parecidas podem dificultar a navegação e interferir em infraestruturas hidrelétricas.

Por enquanto, a B.C. Hydro não considera necessárias medidas drásticas, embora continue monitorando novas imagens de satélite e possíveis avisos da população.

Já Gammer foi direto ao se dirigir aos curiosos: aproximem-se de barco, tirem fotos, usem drones, mas não tentem pisar na ilha.

articles.summary: g1 fez uma seleção das atrações culturais pagas e gratuitas na região entre 4 e 6 de setembro.
articles.body:
Fim de semana, véspera de feriado, recheado de atrações culturais no Sul de Minas. Há opções de shows de rock, MPB e sertanejo, festivais gastronômicos, encontro de tatuagem e lançamento de livro.

Vai ter shows gratuitos do Barão Vermelho e Vanessa da Mata, em Campanha ; de Sérgio Reis e Édson Hudson em Natércia , e de Munhoz & Mariano em Elói Mendes .

articles.title: Israel afirma que consolidou 'zona de segurança' no sul do Líbano | G1
articles.standfirst: Exército israelense diz ter concluído consolidação da área ocupada no sul do Líbano após assumir controle de colina estratégica usada pelo Hezbollah.
articles.summary: Exército israelense diz ter concluído consolidação da área ocupada no sul do Líbano após assumir controle de colina estratégica usada pelo Hezbollah.
articles.body:
Um comboio do Comitê Internacional da Cruz Vermelha (CICV) percorre uma estrada no sul do Líbano, a caminho de um ponto de encontro para receber quatro pessoas que haviam sido detidas em Israel. — Foto: KAWNAT HAJU/AFP

Israel afirmou nesta sexta-feira, 4, que consolidou a "zona de segurança" que ocupa no sul do Líbano após tomar uma colina que servia de posição estratégica para o movimento pró-iraniano Hezbollah .

O Exército israelense anunciou na quinta-feira que assumiu o controle da colina, situada ao norte do rio Litani e no limite da zona ocupada por Israel no sul do Líbano.

"A tomada da colina de Ali Taher marca a conclusão da fase de consolidação do controle na zona de segurança no sul do Líbano", afirmou o ministro da Defesa, Israel Katz.

Segundo o governo de Israel, o Hezbollah havia cavado túneis no setor, o que possibilitava o lançamento de drones e mísseis contra posições militares israelenses no sul do Líbano, assim como contra o norte de Israel, do outro lado da fronteira.

O Exército israelense "vai agora concluir a neutralização dos túneis e se preparar, da maneira tática apropriada, para manter o controle da colina e impedir que o inimigo volte a se estabelecer na área", disse Katz.

"Israel não vai se retirar da zona de segurança no Líbano até que o Hezbollah seja desarmado", insistiu o ministro israelense da Defesa.

Em março, o Hezbollah lançou ataques contra Israel em solidariedade com o Irã e arrastou o Líbano à guerra, mas a violência diminuiu desde o acordo entre Irã e Estados Unidos em junho, paralelamente a um acordo entre Líbano e Israel.

Antes de escolher onde estudar, conhecer a estrutura e entender as possibilidades oferecidas pela universidade podem ajudar na tomada de decisão — Foto: Marcel Sabatino

O professor de matemática Gabriel reuniu dicas importantes sobre estatística e análise de dados para estudantes que vão fazer o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) este ano. Aproveitando o contexto do ano eleitoral, o foco da aula é entender como gráficos, pesquisas e margens de erro aparecem nas provas e no cotidiano.

Na videoaula do Lá Vem o Enem , Gabriel explica que a estatística é uma ferramenta central para interpretar dados políticos e que pequenos detalhes em gráficos podem distorcer a realidade.

“É preciso sempre prestar atenção nos eixos dos gráficos. Às vezes o eixo é alterado e não começa do zero, o que é o correto, dando uma falsa sensação visual de grande diferença entre os candidatos para confundir o eleitor”, alerta o professor.

Para simplificar conceitos que costumam cair no exame, Gabriel explica na prática a diferença entre população e amostra estatística, além de resolver uma questão sobre margem de erro em pesquisas eleitorais.

Ciee está com 188 vagas de estágio e jovem aprendiz no Alto Tietê — Foto: Bruna Bonfim/g1

O Centro de Integração Empresa - Escola (Ciee) tem 188 vagas no Alto Tietê nesta sexta-feira (4).

Deste total, 162 são para estágio e 26 para jovem aprendiz . As oportunidades são para estudantes do ensino médio, técnico e superior.

As vagas são em Mogi das Cruzes , Suzano , Guararema e Poá . As principais áreas contratando para estágio são administração e marketing. Para jovem aprendiz é administração.

Para se candidatar é necessário realizar o cadastro no portal do Ciee e o CEP, e-mail e número de contato precisam estar corretos.

Na plataforma o candidato pode fazer cursos e enriquecer o currículo, com avaliação por meio de vídeo-apresentação e redação online. Todas as ferramentas são disponibilizadas gratuitamente.

articles.standfirst: Novo jato leve da Embraer poderá levar até 10 passageiros, voar a mais de 800 km/h e realizar pouso de emergência de forma automática.
articles.summary: Novo jato leve da Embraer poderá levar até 10 passageiros, voar a mais de 800 km/h e realizar pouso de emergência de forma automática.
articles.body:
Mais conforto, mais segurança e voos diretos para todas as capitais do país: essas são as promessas do novo jato leve Phenom 300EV, modelo da Embraer capaz de realizar pousos por conta própria.

Previsto para começar a ser entregue em 2028, ele foi anunciado em julho . Em agosto, recebeu certificação da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) e de autoridades de aviação nos Estados Unidos e na União Europeia.

O Phenom 300EV terá espaço para até 10 passageiros, além de um piloto, e poderá ter a configuração dos assentos personalizada pelo proprietário.

O jato foi certificado para fazer voos com dois ou apenas um piloto. E, segundo a Embraer, este é o modelo de piloto único mais rápido e com mais alcance no mercado.

Imagem de conceito do Phenom 300EV, jato leve da Embraer — Foto: Divulgação/Embraer

As especificações apontam que o Phenom 300EV terá velocidade máxima de 0,8 Mach (ou 0,8 vez a velocidade do som), o que, na altitude de cruzeiro (45 mil pés ou 13,7 mil metros) representa cerca de 859 km/h.

A aeronave terá autonomia de até 3.805 km, que permite voos diretos para as capitais de todos os estados brasileiros , bem como a cidades como La Paz, Santiago e Buenos Aires a partir de São Paulo.

A Embraer destaca três configurações de assentos que variam de 7 a 10 passageiros.

Com a capacidade máxima, os voos têm apenas um piloto, a poltrona do copiloto é ocupada por um passageiro e um cinto de segurança é colocado até mesmo no assento do lavatório.

A fabricante permitirá personalizar as poltronas, os pisos e as mesas embutidas para os passageiros. A cabine contará ainda com painéis para os próprios passageiros controlarem temperatura, iluminação e áudio.

Ainda segundo a Embraer, o Phenom 300EV tem as maiores janelas de sua categoria, conexão com internet de satélites de órbita baixa e um sistema de ionização de ar.

Segundo a Embraer, o Phenom 300EV será o primeiro jato leve com o sistema de pouso automático da empresa americana de tecnologia Garmin , que pode ser ativada manual ou automaticamente caso o piloto não consiga completar o voo.

Batizado de Emergency Autoland, o sistema encontra o aeroporto mais adequado para o pouso considerando fatores como distância e autonomia de combustível e sinaliza a rota para o controle de tráfego aéreo e os passageiros.

A aeronave conta ainda com um sistema de freio automático, que oferece pousos mais suaves, e um sistema de alerta para evitar saídas da pista.

No final de agosto, o Phenom 100, um modelo da Embraer classificado como um jato muito leve, saiu da pista no Aeroporto Santos Dumont, no Rio de Janeiro e afetou mais de 80 voos .

A fabricante afirma que os recursos de segurança do Phenom 300EV são possibilitados por um novo computador de bordo que controla funções da aeronave eletronicamente e reduz a carga de trabalho de pilotos.

articles.title: ‘Feel the power’: Swatantra Bhardwaj's Instagram story after ‘cracking CJP protester’s skull’ at Jantar Mantar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: “Feel the power!” influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj posted a photograph flaunting his kada on Instagram, days after allegedly boasting in a pod.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: “Feel the power!” influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj posted a photograph flaunting his kada on Instagram, days after allegedly boasting in a podcast about “cracking” the skull of a CJP protester’s father during a scuffle at Jantar Mantar.The Instagram story came around the time Delhi Police issued a clarification on the case, saying Sanjay Kumar, father of student protester Nishu Azad, suffered a head injury during the CJP protest but rejecting claims that his skull had been fractured.In the podcast video that triggered a political row, Bhardwaj is heard claiming, “I cracked the skull of Nishu's father,” while alleging that his political connections had helped him avoid jail.He claimed that a call from Delhi minister Kapil Mishra had helped him remain free and referred to Mishra, Chirag Paswan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi as his “elder brothers”, claiming to enjoy their support.Delhi Police rejected allegations of political interference as “factually incorrect and baseless”, saying due legal action had been taken against Bhardwaj and another accused.According to police, Kumar, 38, a Ghaziabad resident, sustained a head injury during a scuffle at the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar on June 23. The injury was caused by a kada worn by one of the alleged assailants and not by a weapon, police said.Kumar was examined at RML Hospital, where his injuries were described as simple in nature. Police said claims that his skull had been fractured were not supported by the medical records.A case was registered at Parliament Street police station based on Kumar's complaint. Police said Suraj Kumar, 24, and Bhardwaj, 21, were detained from the protest site, served notices and interrogated during the investigation.“Due legal action has been taken, and chargesheet would be filed before the competent court soon,” police said, adding that the matter had been handled strictly according to law and procedure.The Cockroach Janta Party, meanwhile, demanded stronger action against Bhardwaj, describing his statements in the podcast as an “open admission”. Party spokesperson Saurav Das said CJP members would visit Parliament Street police station on Friday to seek justice for Kumar and his daughter Nishu.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also questioned why Bhardwaj had allegedly remained free despite his purported statements in the video. AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal and TMC MP Mahua Moitra also targeted the BJP over the controversy.Nishu, who has expressed concerns about her family's safety, said she would continue her fight against injustice and casteism and would join her father during the visit to the police station.Police have maintained that there was no undue influence or interference in the case and said a chargesheet would be filed before the competent court soon.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Janmashtami 2026: 5 remedies to seek Krishna’s blessings in life
articles.summary: Rituals & Puja News: Janmashtami 2026 is very special. The Moon will be exalted in Taurus and placed in Rohini Nakshatra, while Jupiter will be exalted in Cancer. Venus wi.
articles.body: Janmashtami 2026 is very special. The Moon will be exalted in Taurus and placed in Rohini Nakshatra, while Jupiter will be exalted in Cancer. Venus will occupy its own sign Libra. These placements favour family happiness, education, relationships and emotional stability.However, Mercury will be combust and Saturn will remain retrograde. This makes reflection and corrective action just as important as celebration.Create a 16-Kala Deep MandalaPlace 16 ghee diyas in a wide circle around Laddu Gopal. The number represents the 16 kalas traditionally associated with the completeness of Krishna’s divine personality.Do not light the lamps hurriedly. With every diya, think of one part of life that needs light, such as health, family, knowledge, confidence, relationships or spiritual growth. Sit quietly before the completed circle for a few minutes.The Sun in Leo supports self-awareness, whereas the exalted Moon encourages emotional completeness. This remedy is particularly suitable for someone who is progressing in one area of life but feels empty or unsettled in another.Use stable metal diyas or place them on fire-resistant trays. Keep them away from clothes, curtains, children and the decorations around the jhula.Write Krishna’s 108 Names by HandTake a clean sheet of paper and write the 108 names of Lord Krishna using blue ink. Do not print the names or ask someone else to write them for you. The movement of your own hand is part of the practice.Mercury will be combust during Janmashtami 2026. This can represent scattered thoughts, communication gaps and difficulty converting knowledge into action. Handwriting slows the mind down. It makes you stay with every name instead of chanting mechanically while thinking about something else.Complete the writing before the midnight puja and place the page near Laddu Gopal. You may later keep it inside your spiritual journal or prayer book.This remedy can be chosen by students, writers, teachers and anyone seeking greater clarity in communication or decision-making.Write a Personal Letter to KrishnaMost prayers tell God what we want. A letter can reveal what we have been avoiding.Write down your biggest worry, one mistake you genuinely recognise and one promise you want to fulfil during the coming year. Then add the first practical step you will take towards correcting the situation.Read the letter privately before Laddu Gopal. It does not need impressive language. Honesty is more valuable here than beautifully written Sanskrit.Retrograde Saturn supports the review of unfinished responsibilities, while the Sun and Ketu in Leo ask us to look beyond pride. Combust Mercury also makes written reflection useful when emotions are difficult to express aloud.Avoid using the letter to demand control over another person. Write about what you can change in your own thoughts, choices and conduct.Support a Child’s Skill EducationKrishna should not receive every offering while a child outside the temple remains unable to study.Help a child purchase books, art material, a musical instrument or equipment needed for a practical skill. You may also contribute towards school fees, digital learning or a course that can improve the child’s future.Jupiter, the planet of knowledge, teachers and children, will be exalted in Cancer. This makes educational support one of the most relevant remedies for Janmashtami 2026.The assistance does not have to be large or public. Even one carefully chosen book can become more valuable than an expensive decorative offering. Give respectfully, without turning the child into content for social media.Take a Joint Jhula Sankalp as a CoupleA couple can sit together and gently swing Laddu Gopal’s jhula during the midnight celebration. Before doing so, each partner should make one realistic promise for the relationship.It could be listening without using the phone, avoiding insults during disagreements, creating time for one weekly meal together or discussing finances more transparently.Venus in its own sign Libra supports partnership, while the exalted Moon in Rohini encourages tenderness and emotional security. The ritual is especially meaningful for couples who love each other but have allowed routine, ego or poor communication to create distance.Do not make dramatic promises that will be forgotten by the following week. Choose something small enough to practise and important enough to matter.Get the latest religion news and spiritual insights. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Canada planted a pine forest where a rare savanna once stood; removing the trees later brought back a richer ecosystem
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A patch of rare savanna habitat in the Ottawa Valley has recovered remarkably well after decades under a planted pine forest, according to a study exa.
articles.body: A patch of rare savanna habitat in the Ottawa Valley has recovered remarkably well after decades under a planted pine forest, according to a study examining restoration efforts at a site called The Sandhills near Constance Bay, Ontario. Researchers from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada compared a cleared hectare, where planted pine trees had been removed and pine litter cleared away, against the surrounding Red Pine plantation still standing nearby. The clearing work itself required only about 5 people working for less than 2 weeks, after which native savanna vegetation largely re-established itself naturally, helped along by seeds drifting in from nearby remnant patches along old paths and firebreaks. Biodiversity in the restored clearing turned out to be substantially higher than in the plantation, with more flowering plants, shrubs and regionally rare species taking hold once the pine canopy and its accumulated litter were finally cleared away for good.How researchers measured savanna restoration success at Constance BayTo evaluate how well the native ecosystem had bounced back, researchers gathered data from quadrats laid out along transects, allowing them to directly compare vegetation in the restored clearing against the adjacent pine plantation. As described in Successful re-establishment of a native savannah flora and fauna on the site of a former pine plantation at Constance Bay, Ottawa, Ontario, the restoration process itself involved cutting and bulldozing the planted trees and stripping away accumulated pine duff and litter, work that took a small team just days to complete across roughly a hectare of land. Beyond a limited seeding effort, the researchers noted that most of the native plant recovery happened on its own, aided significantly by seed dispersal from surviving pockets of remnant vegetation scattered nearby.Why the pine plantation struggled to support native savanna speciesThe comparison between the 2 sites revealed clear differences in ecological health. While the semi-open Jack Pine plantation supported a mix of species adapted to both shaded and open conditions, with diversity levels approaching those found in the clearing, some native plants fared poorly under the pine canopy. Blueberry plants growing within the plantation, for example, were generally found in poor condition and largely failed to produce flowers or fruit, a sign that the altered light and soil conditions beneath the pines were suppressing natural reproductive cycles that once defined this landscape before commercial forestry arrived.What the results suggest about future savanna restoration effortsThe restored clearing consistently outperformed the plantation across nearly every biodiversity measure the researchers tracked, showing greater development of flowering herbaceous plants and shrubs alongside a noticeably higher number of regionally rare species. Orthopteran insects, a group that includes grasshoppers and crickets and serves as a useful indicator of overall plant feeding diversity, were also markedly more abundant and varied within the restored area compared with the surrounding pines. The researchers concluded that savanna and natural sand barren habitats destroyed by plantation forestry can be restored both successfully and inexpensively, suggesting there is little reason such efforts could not be expanded to cover much larger areas across similarly affected landscapes in the future.Why the Constance Bay restoration mattersThe results are particularly notable because the researchers achieved the recovery with relatively little intervention. Once the planted pines and accumulated duff were removed, the site was able to regain much of its native vegetation without extensive planting or intensive management. The authors suggest that nearby remnants of the original savanna, including vegetation along paths and firebreaks, provided an important source of seeds for recolonisation. That finding points to the value of protecting small surviving patches of native habitat, which can help surrounding areas recover when damaging land uses are removed. The study was also significant because it showed that restoration did not necessarily require costly replanting across the entire site. Instead, removing the conditions that had suppressed the original ecosystem allowed native plants and insects to return largely on their own. The researchers argued that similar restoration could be considered across larger areas of savanna and natural sand barren affected by plantation forestry.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Watch: 2 workers make it out alive 9 days after Nepal floods hit hydropower tunnel
articles.summary: South Asia News: Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Friday, nine days after devastating floods and lands.
articles.body: Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Friday, nine days after devastating floods and landslides trapped hundreds of workers inside tunnels across several hydropower sites.The rescue brought a dramatic breakthrough to a desperate operation, but hopes of finding more survivors rose further after rescuers heard voices coming from inside the tunnel, according to Bipin Regmi, police chief in the flood-hit district of Nuwakot.“Rescuers heard voices,” Regmi told CNN, adding that a medical team was on its way to the site.The two workers were pulled out in quick succession from inside the Trishuli 3A plant, where rescuers have been boring into a tunnel in an effort to reach 42 workers who had remained unaccounted for.Video showed about a dozen rescuers pulling one man through a small opening in the ground and clapping as he emerged. The mud-covered worker was then carried away on a rescuer’s shoulder, while a medical team checked on him.Nepal Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first rescue during the operation. Nepal lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane later said a second worker had also been rescued alive.The tunnel leading to the underground powerhouse is more than 4 kilometres (2.5 miles) long. Dozens of workers were inside when the catastrophic flooding hit the area.About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, according to local authorities, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped inside tunnels. Among those unaccounted for are workers from China, South Korea and India.Read more: Nepal estimates $2.56 billion flood damage, faces $52.6 million recovery costThe rescue effort has continued under treacherous conditions since Aug. 26, when massive floods and landslides tore through parts of Nepal, likely after a glacier collapse. At least 1,259 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.On the Tibet side of the border, China said late Wednesday that 21 people had been killed and 541 were missing.The chances of finding survivors have become increasingly uncertain with each passing day. Indian Army Colonel Parikshit Mehra, who was involved in the rescue operation at the Trishuli 3A site, said earlier this week that the first 48 hours are the most crucial in a tunnel rescue.“People who are stuck tend to panic much more than when they are outside in the open,” Mehra told CNN’s Anderson Cooper.“Getting stuck in a tunnel you can’t see anything. Generally if you stay in the dark you get disoriented in about 24-25 hours,” he said.“Beyond that, (after) 48 hours, you start hallucinating. And then I think from there on it’s always a fight.”Yet, even as the operation entered its ninth day, Mehra offered a note of hope saying, “There have been miracles.”Also read: Nepal minister goes back on flash flood 'compensation' claimThe flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, caused widespread destruction across northern and central Nepal, killing at least 1,282 people and leaving thousands missing. Nepal Police said the highest number of recovered bodies were reported from Chitwan, Nawalparasi East and West, Nuwakot and Rasuwa, with rescue and recovery operations continuing across the affected areas.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Thai ice cream founder has put his 27-year-old business up for roughly $6 million after deciding to become a monk
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Siripong Akkarasriyuk built Hawell’s at a time when ice cream shops were becoming a familiar sight in Thailand’s shopping centres. He knew the trade f.
articles.body: Siripong Akkarasriyuk built Hawell’s at a time when ice cream shops were becoming a familiar sight in Thailand’s shopping centres. He knew the trade from the ground up, having worked as an ice cream seller before launching his own brand in 1999. The first Hawell’s outlet opened at Central Pinklao, and the business expanded quickly, reaching 22 branches within three years. Its fortunes later changed. Competition intensified, branches closed and attempts to secure new space in shopping malls repeatedly ran into difficulties. According to Bangkok Post, Hawell’s eventually returned with a standalone shop in 2023, but only one outlet remains today.Now, Siripong is preparing to leave the business behind. Reportedly,he has offered Hawell’s for sale for 165 million baht as he plans to enter monkhood. The move has been years in the making, with the businessman saying he wants to devote the next chapter of his life to Buddhist practice.The Thai ice cream brand expanded rapidly before its fortunes changedSiripong’s connection with the trade began well before Hawell’s existed. He had worked as an ice cream seller and later became known through Thai television programmes focused on entrepreneurs.When Hawell’s opened its first shop at Central Pinklao in December 1999, the brand quickly found an audience. Within three years, it had grown to 22 branches, establishing a presence in shopping centres and becoming one of the more recognisable Thai ice cream names of that period.The business was built around relatively affordable ice cream and, for a time, its expansion appeared to be gathering pace.The brand slowly lost its place in shopping mallsHawell’s struggled to maintain its network of branches as larger ice cream companies strengthened their relationships with shopping centres. Siripong has said that some rivals secured exclusive arrangements that made it difficult for competing brands to secure space in the same locations.Reportedly, its original Central Pinklao outlet eventually closed in 2014, and the brand was left trying to find a way back into a market it had once occupied quite comfortably.Siripong continued to explore expansion. Over the past two years, he said, Hawell’s approached shopping malls about opening new outlets but repeatedly received the same response: there was no available space. This was despite vacant units being left behind by businesses that had already moved out.Opening more standalone shops was possible, but it would require substantial investment. Franchising was also considered, although Siripong was reluctant to pursue rapid growth that might put the brand under pressure.In 2023, Hawell’s returned with a standalone shop in Bang Bua Thong, in Nonthaburi. It is now the company's only operating branch.Siripong’s plans to become a monk are behind the saleHe has been considering monastic life for more than 15 years and says he has given himself a two-year period to put his affairs in order before taking that step.His intention is not simply to retire from Hawell’s. He wants to leave ordinary business and family life behind and dedicate himself to Buddhist practice.Siripong has also written about Buddhism. His 2016 book, Success Derived from the Buddha, explored Buddhist teachings, and he has spoken publicly about the subject over the years.Siripong wants to build a forest retreat before becoming a monkThe next two years are expected to be spent preparing for a very different kind of life.Siripong says he wants to acquire land and establish a forest sanctuary where he can meditate and live away from the routines of his previous life. Once he enters monkhood, he plans to cut off regular contact with family and friends as he pursues what he describes as the ultimate aim of becoming an arahant.He has spoken about eventually returning to wider society only to help teach Buddhist practice to his wife, daughter, relatives and disciples.What the buyer will getThe asking price is 165 million baht, or roughly $6 million. The proposed sale covers considerably more than the Hawell’s name itself.Included in the deal is the company's office and factory, machinery and licences, as well as the existing Hawell’s Ice Cream & Fast Food outlet. The buyer would also acquire the trademark, business know-how and the recipes used to make its ice cream.Siripong is actively looking for a successor rather than simply placing the company on the market and stepping away. He has offered a referral payment of 5 million baht to anyone who introduces a buyer who completes the deal at the asking price.Siripong still wants Hawell’s to surviveDespite deciding to give up the company, Siripong has said he does not want Hawell’s to disappear with his departure.The brand has been part of his working life since the late 1990s, through its rapid expansion, the closure of its branches and its more recent attempt to establish itself again with a standalone shop.Finding a successor is now the final piece of that transition. Siripong hopes someone will take the business on and continue developing it, while he turns his attention to the forest retreat and the religious life he has been preparing for over many years.“Even if I choose to leave worldly life behind … I still want to see Hawell’s move forward.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘World has reached the moon, we still carry children’: 80-year wait for bridge in Chhattisgarh's Sonpal village
articles.summary: RAIPUR: “The world has reached the moon, but we still carry our children on our shoulders across the stream to help them reach school.” That is how re.
articles.body: RAIPUR: “The world has reached the moon, but we still carry our children on our shoulders across the stream to help them reach school.” That is how residents of remote Sonpal village in Durgukondal block of Kanker district describe an eight-decade wait for a bridge they say has been promised by successive governments but never built.For villagers, the missing bridge is not merely an infrastructure gap. During the rains, it determines whether children can reach school, whether families can travel for work or treatment, and whether anyone can cross the village boundary without risking a fall into the swollen stream.Videos of parents carrying children on their shoulders through the flooded crossing have surfaced on social media, drawing attention to the village’s daily struggle.One of the women said villagers had even travelled to the state capital with applications seeking a bridge, but nothing changed. “It feels as if we are still not part of independent India,” she said.“The four months of monsoon are the worst. If someone falls ill, an ambulance cannot reach us. Children miss school, and sometimes their books get washed away in the water,” she said. “How are our children supposed to go to school? If they have to attend, the only option is for parents to carry them on their shoulders, otherwise their uniforms get soaked and covered in mud. They fall and others are so short, they can't stand in that water. Who would understand our pain? A bridge has to be built here.”Village head Sanuram Dugga said generations have lived with the same demand. “Our fathers and grandfathers kept asking for this bridge and died waiting. Now our generation is asking for it,” he said. “Governments come and go— everyone said it would be built. The promises were made, not the bridge.”A 2.3km blacktop road, constructed about three years ago at a cost of crores, exists on both sides of the stream. But in between, the road gets inundated during the monsoon.During the monsoon, villagers say adults wade across at considerable risk, while younger children are carried on shoulders or backs to get them safely to the other side.Women in the village — Iswanti Rana, Subhadra Patel, Sagro Bai Dugga, Basanti Kumeti and Somari Yadav — said they have heard the same assurance since they got married in Sonpal: “The bridge will be built this year.” Now, their children are bearing the brunt.Residents say the absence of a crossing affects not only schoolchildren but anyone needing to reach markets, hospitals, workplaces or government offices outside the village.Mahendra Singh Thakur, a sub-engineer with the Bridge Corporation in Kanker, told reporters that the Sonpal bridge has been included in the 2026-27 budget and that a fresh estimate will now be prepared and forwarded for further action.For Sonpal, however, an estimate is still not a bridge.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Raipur | Silver Rate in Raipur | Bank Holidays in Raipur | Public Holidays in Raipur | Raipur AQI | Weather in Raipur | Petrol Price in Raipur | Diesel Price in Raipur | CNG Price in Raipur | LPG Price in RaipurStay updated with the latest Raipur news. articles.title: HarperCollins to publish Sonia Gandhi’s controversial memoir
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: So, who does Sonia Gandhi’s controversial memoir ‘Belonging’ belong to? HarperCollins India has stepped in to publish the Congress leader’s.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: So, who does Sonia Gandhi’s controversial memoir ‘Belonging’ belong to? HarperCollins India has stepped in to publish the Congress leader’s memoir, ending weeks of uncertainty over who would carry the domestic edition after Penguin Random House India (PRHI) exited the deal over some changes to the text. The book will hit Indian shelves on November 10, 2026 — the same day as its international release.Billed as one of the most anticipated political memoirs in recent years, Belonging is described as a personal account of love, identity, duty and belonging, offering an insider's perspective on India's political journey through Gandhi's own eyes.The HarperCollins announcement comes on the heels of a public controversy over PRHI's departure from the project, which Congress leaders have framed as an act of political censorship. Party leader Ashok Gehlot alleged that pressure had been exerted on Penguin to edit out sections dealing with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the RSS, and China's occupation of Indian territory during Modi's tenure, calling the episode a "murder of democracy."Penguin pushed back on that framing, maintaining that it retained the right to fact-check manuscripts and suggest edits to authors, and said it remained open to publishing the book. The company had earlier this year also halted distribution of cartoonist Joe Sacco's The Once and Future Riot, about the Muzaffarnagar riots — a decision critics have pointed to as part of a pattern.Adding a layer of intrigue to the row was the fact that Alfred A. Knopf, the memoir's American publisher, is itself a Penguin Random House imprint — raising the question, as Gehlot put it, of why a version cleared for global release would need alteration for Indian readers. "What is the reason, or what pressure is there that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?" he asked.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi, who was questioned by Delhi Police's special cell for several hours Wednesday, said he and his lawyers were yet to be pro-vided with a copy of the FIR against him.Speaking to TOI, Joshi, a 1992-batch officer of the Indian Post and Telecommunication Accounts and Finance Service, said he went to Delhi Police headquarters Thursday with a letter from his lawyers asking that he be provided with a copy of the FIR against him. The FIR has been registered under section 192 of Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita, which relates to "wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot".Joshi said he was approached by two Delhi Police officers as he was leaving Nehru Park Wednesday morning."They showed me the first page of the FIR for a short while. It mentioned a post I had made on X on Aug 26 about SIR and elections in West Bengal. I was not shown the second page of the FIR; so, I am at the police headquarters with a letter from my lawyers to seek a copy, which they are required to provide to me," Joshi said.Police sources said as Joshi was not arrested and only questioned, there was no need to provide a copy of the FIR at this stage.Sources said that the cops questioned him regarding his post on X that called for "Nuremberg style trial" - military tribunals held after World War II - of the chief election commission in connection with the West Bengal elections while demanding that they be held again.During questioning, Joshi claimed, he was asked about his social media activity, including his post on the chief election commissioner and another he made on Aug 13.Earlier in the day, Joshi posted on X that he was not allowed to inform his family and friends that he was being questioned by police offi-cials Wednesday."Informing an individual's family during interrogation or detention is a legal mandate, not an optional courtesy... I was only permitted to make a call at 6.38pm, leaving my family & friends in total panic the entire day," he posted on X, tagging Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar.Delhi Police, however, rejected the allegations, asserting that all mandated legal provisions were followed during the questioning. Police said that following their request to join the investigation, Joshi came to the special cell's office in New Friends Colony in his own vehicle and was escorted home safely and cordially in the evening.Sources in Delhi Police had said Wednesday that Joshi and his wife were duly informed about the questioning and the registration of an FIR.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Quote of the day by Beyoncé: “Don't try to lessen yourself...” - a powerful lesson on self-belief and authenticity
articles.summary: US News: There is a difference between adapting to the world and reducing yourself to fit it. Beyoncé’s widely shared advice, “Don't try to lessen yourself for.
articles.body: There is a difference between adapting to the world and reducing yourself to fit it. Beyoncé’s widely shared advice, “Don't try to lessen yourself for the world; let the world catch up to you,” speaks directly to that tension. On the surface, it sounds like confidence: do not become smaller simply because other people are not ready for what you bring. Beneath that is a demanding idea about patience, self-knowledge and the courage to keep developing work or an identity that may not receive immediate approval. Coming from an artist whose career has repeatedly tested the boundaries of genre and popular expectation, the line carries particular weight. It asks a difficult question: when the world does not immediately understand you, should you change yourself—or give it time to understand?Quote of the day by Beyoncé“Don't try to lessen yourself for the world; let the world catch up to you.” Where this line actually comes fromThe quote is often circulated online as a standalone Beyoncé saying, but its clearest documented context comes through Chloe and Halle Bailey, the sister duo Beyoncé mentored and signed to Parkwood Entertainment. In a 2017 interview discussed by Essence, the sisters described Beyoncé as encouraging them to remain true to themselves, with Chloe recalling her advice: “Don't try to lessen yourself for the world; let the world catch up to you.” Around the same period, Halle told W Magazine that Beyoncé’s message was to let the world catch up rather than “dumb” their music down, after the young artists had heard that their work might be too complex for an average listener. A 2018 Nylon profile recorded a closely related version of the advice. The available reporting therefore places the line in the context of Beyoncé mentoring younger artists and protecting their creative individuality, rather than in a public speech or published essay. That matters because the sentence was not simply abstract encouragement; it was advice about what to do when originality creates pressure to become more conventional.What the quote actually meansThe key word in the quote is “lessen.” Beyoncé is not saying that people should refuse criticism, reject growth or assume that every idea they have is ahead of its time. She is warning against a different impulse: deliberately reducing your ability, ambition, identity or creative instincts simply to become easier for others to accept. “Let the world catch up” introduces patience into the idea. Recognition does not always arrive at the same moment as originality. A student may have an unconventional career goal, an artist may create work that does not fit familiar categories, or an employee may approach a problem differently from the accepted method. The quote suggests that unfamiliarity is not, by itself, evidence that something is wrong. The harder task is learning to distinguish useful feedback, which can improve you, from pressure that merely asks you to become less distinctive.Why this idea still matters todayThat distinction is especially relevant in a culture shaped by algorithms, trends and instant reaction. Social media can reward recognisable formats quickly, while unusual work may need more time to find an audience. The same pressure appears at work and in education, where people can feel pushed to sound, dress, create or behave in ways that already seem acceptable. Beyoncé’s line offers a useful counterweight: immediate approval should not become the only test of value. Adapting a presentation, learning from criticism or improving a skill can be sensible; erasing the quality that makes the work yours is different. The challenge is to remain flexible about method without becoming uncertain about identity.Self-belief does not mean rejecting criticismRefusing to make yourself smaller should not be confused with believing you are beyond correction. Healthy self-belief can coexist with rigorous self-editing and difficult feedback. Beyoncé has spoken about being highly critical of her work and pushing herself creatively, while also insisting that she must ultimately make her own decisions. That combination changes the meaning of the quote. The point is not “ignore everyone.” It is to know which compromises improve the work and which remove the quality that made it worth doing.The world may need time to understand something newNew ideas often look less strange after people have had time to encounter them. Music, fashion, technology and workplace habits can move from unfamiliar to mainstream once audiences understand their value. That does not make every unconventional idea successful, but it explains why instant acceptance can be a poor measure of potential. Sometimes resistance calls for revision; at other times, it calls for consistency long enough for understanding to catch up.Beyoncé’s career gives the words added weightBeyoncé’s career gives the advice added weight. Her work has crossed music, visual storytelling and business ownership, while projects such as Cowboy Carter challenged familiar genre boundaries. At the 2025 Grammys, the album won Album of the Year and Best Country Album, making Beyoncé the first Black woman to win the latter category. She now holds 35 Grammys, the most of any artist.Confidence still has to be backed by workSelf-belief becomes convincing only when supported by work. In her 2020 “Dear Class of 2020” address, Beyoncé paired authenticity with effort, failure, accountability and respect. That puts an important limit on the quote: asking the world to catch up is not permission to stand still. It means developing the discipline and skill that make confidence more than a pose.Other memorable quotes by Beyoncé“The world will respect you as much as you respect yourself.” “You can decide what success looks like for yourself.” “I have learnt that my voice is clearer when I am still.” “I push them and I push myself. It’s just who I am.” How to apply this quote in daily lifeStart by noticing the moments when you make yourself smaller before anyone has asked you to. You may stay quiet in a meeting despite having a useful idea, hide an ambitious goal because friends may find it unrealistic, or simplify creative work because it does not resemble what is popular. Ask whether the change improves what you are doing or merely makes it safer and more familiar. Listen seriously to criticism and revise when it identifies a real weakness. But if the only objection is that your direction is unusual, give it enough time and work to prove itself. The aim is not to resist the world; it is to stop confusing acceptance with worth.Why these words still resonateThe lasting appeal of Beyoncé’s words lies in a choice most people face: belonging quickly or remaining recognisably themselves. The pressure may appear in a career, classroom, relationship or creative pursuit, and it rarely arrives as a direct demand to become smaller. More often, it appears as an invitation to be quieter, safer or more predictable. “Let the world catch up to you” does not guarantee that others will agree or applaud. Instead, it offers permission to let recognition take time while continuing to improve and trust what is genuinely yours. The goal is not to be different for its own sake, but to avoid abandoning something valuable simply because others have not learned how to see it.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: FBI adds India-origin man Manjit Singh Bedi to most-wanted fraudsters list, offers reward up to $150k for info
articles.summary: US & Canada News News: The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has added India-born Manjit Singh Bedi to its most-wanted fraudsters list over his alleged role in a sche.
articles.body: The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has added India-born Manjit Singh Bedi to its most-wanted fraudsters list over his alleged role in a scheme that defrauded the US government of at least $600,000 in SNAP benefits between March 2024 and June 2025.According to the FBI, Bedi, a naturalised US citizen, operated Asian Grocery Store in Tacoma, Washington, where he allegedly used customers' Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards to process transactions without providing food. Instead, he is accused of giving SNAP participants cash and keeping half of the proceeds.“Instead of selling participants food, Bedi is alleged to have swiped their cards and given them cash,” the FBI said in its wanted notice.Bedi was indicted on charges of wire fraud and SNAP benefits fraud but was allowed to appear in court without being arrested. He was ordered to surrender his passport and remain in Washington state. The FBI said he later drove into Canada and fled to India.A federal arrest warrant was issued for Bedi on May 21, 2026, in the US District Court for the Western District of Washington after he was charged with violations of conditions of supervision. The FBI said he is currently believed to be residing in India.The agency is offering a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to Bedi's arrest and conviction.

articles.title: Take Me Home, Country Roads singer John Denver bought 957 Colorado acres in 1979; Windstar later sold, but 927 wildlife-habitat acres stayed protected
articles.summary: US News: John Denver bought a 957-acre property in Old Snowmass, Colorado, in 1979 and had a vision of it becoming the home of the Windstar Foundation, which w.
articles.body: John Denver bought a 957-acre property in Old Snowmass, Colorado, in 1979 and had a vision of it becoming the home of the Windstar Foundation, which was an environmental organization he had co-founded three years earlier. The property was sold after decades, but most of the land remained protected under a conservation easement that prevents development on 927 acres.The Windstar property sits in the Roaring Fork Valley, about 10 miles north of Aspen. The land had been used as a sheep ranch and later became a retreat center for St. Benedict's Monastery, following which Denver bought it in 1979 and developed the property as the base for his environmental work. The official John Denver website records the purchase and later conservation history.Denver's environmental project took shapeDenver co-founded the Windstar Foundation in 1976 as a nonprofit environmental education and research center. The foundation focused on conservation and environmental issues, and the Old Snowmass property became closely associated with that work. The land was more than a private mountain retreat, since Denver envisioned an environmental research facility there, with space for staff and programs connected to the Windstar Foundation.The property eventually became the focus of a partnership with the Rocky Mountain Institute, and in 1996, RMI acquired an interest in the land, and the Windstar Land Conservancy was formed by the foundation and RMI to own and manage the property. That same year brought the legal protection that would outlast the organizations' later changes.927 acres were protected from developmentA conservation easement was placed on 927 of the property's 957 acres in 1996, which was held by the Aspen Valley Land Trust and Pitkin County Open Space and Trails. The property was being prepared for sale in 2013, and the distinction between the protected land and the remaining 30 acres became important. The 927 acres could no longer be developed under the terms of the easement.The Aspen Times reported in April 2013 that the easement restricted development on the 927 acres and allowed activities including wildlife-habitat management, agriculture and irrigation. The easement also included a guarantee of public access, wherein visitors were able to use an established route along Windwalker's Ditch. Windstar Land Conservancy officials said the conservation easement could not be altered and would remain in place in perpetuity, which meant that the sale of the property would not automatically open the protected acreage to construction.Windstar was sold in 2013By 2012, the Windstar Foundation was winding down, and its board voted to dissolve the organization, while its conservation work was expected to continue through the Windstar Land Conservancy and its partners. The following year, the 957-acre property was placed under contract for sale to a private buyer. The buyer's identity was not initially disclosed.Earlier plans had included a research center of more than 20,000 square feet and housing for as many as 20 employees. The Rocky Mountain Institute had tried unsuccessfully to obtain county approval for the institutional project in 2004, and by 2013, that plan had been abandoned. The Aspen Times reported that the conservation easement covered 927 acres while the remaining 30 acres were outside its protection. The conservancy ultimately decided not to seek approval for a proposed single-family home on that portion before the sale, which left any future application to the new owner.The land's conservation status survived the saleThe Windstar Land Conservancy and Rocky Mountain Institute announced the sale in April 2013. Their statement was reproduced on Denver's official website, which said the property totaled 957 acres and described it as important wildlife and wetlands habitat. It also confirmed that the 1996 conservation easement protected 927 acres from development forever. The easement was held by Aspen Valley Land Trust and Pitkin County Open Space and Trails. The protected acreage therefore did not disappear when ownership changed, as the legal conservation arrangement remained attached to the land.Denver died in 1997, years before the property was sold. A 2012 statement from the Windstar Foundation said Denver had wanted the land conserved and protected in perpetuity, and described the creation of the Windstar Land Conservancy and conservation easement as fulfilling that intention.Today, the 957-acre property could change hands, but the conservation easement placed on 927 acres was designed to remain in force regardless of the sale. That left the majority of the land under permanent development restrictions while preserving its wildlife, wetland, and open-space functions.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
