articles.title: In 2021, British sculptor Jason deCaires Taylor submerged six giant faces off Cannes; the degraded seabed became a free museum later linked to Posidonia seagrass restoration.
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover the unique underwater museum created by British sculptor Jason deCaires Taylor near Cannes, France. This innovative project features giant submerged faces and aims to revitalize marine life and Posidonia seagrass through art and ecological restoration.
articles.body: In 2021, six enormous faces appeared beneath the Mediterranean off Cannes, France, where visitors could swim over an underwater museum instead of walking through galleries. Created by British sculptor Jason deCaires Taylor, the two-metre-tall sculptures were lowered into the sea near Île Sainte-Marguerite, transforming an environmentally degraded patch of seabed into an unusual meeting point between art and marine conservation. The project was designed not only to give Cannes a new cultural attraction, but also to encourage marine life to return to the area.According to the City of Cannes, the six sculptures were submerged on January 28, 2021, near Île Sainte-Marguerite, at depths of 3 to 5 metres and between 84 and 132 metres from the shore, making them accessible to snorkellers. Each two-metre-high sculpture weighs about 10 tonnes and was made from an ecological, pH-neutral marine material designed to provide refuge for underwater life and eventually function as an artificial reef.From Cannes residents to underwater sculpturesThe artist did not create imaginary faces for the exhibition. Instead, he made moulds of faces belonging to local Cannes residents. During a temporary workshop in 2018, Taylor and his assistants made 45 casts from volunteers, from which six people were selected as models for the sculptures. The chosen participants represented a range of ages and occupations, including a fisherman, student, schoolgirl and cultural mediator, giving the installation a strong connection to the local community without suggesting that six individuals represent the entire townBut the sculptures were never intended to remain pristine artworks. From the outset, their rough surfaces and small cavities were designed to provide places where marine organisms could attach and where fish and shellfish could find shelter. The City of Cannes says the structures were created to evolve into artificial reefs, with algae, shells, corals and benthic fauna gradually colonising their surfaces and becoming part of the local ecosystem. That transformation is no longer merely a future expectation. In 2024, the city reported that all six sculptures had been fully colonised by marine biodiversity, with algae and shells covering their surfaces. The museum was therefore designed as a living installation, where biological growth is part of the artwork rather than something to be removed.Why Posidonia matters beneath the museumHowever, the environmental narrative goes beyond these six sculptures. Previously, the area was quite degraded, and the whole project was designed to attract the return of marine life and plant forms. Posidonia oceanica is the native seagrass of the Mediterranean, which plays an important role since its meadows serve as habitat for marine creatures and contribute to carbon dioxide storage.Research published in Marine Pollution Bulletin identified 25 ecosystem services associated with Posidonia oceanica meadows, including benefits linked to biodiversity, fisheries and coastal environments. The study also highlighted the continuing regression of these meadows despite their protected status, underscoring why protecting and restoring them has become an important Mediterranean conservation goal. The Cannes project has since moved beyond simply placing sculptures on the seabed. In 2024, the city announced the PRIME programme, led by the association NaturDive, to replant 3,000 square metres of Posidonia meadow over three years around the underwater museum. Cannes described the museum site as a suitable laboratory for the restoration experiment because the sculptures had already become colonised by marine biodiversity. This distinction matters as the sculptures themselves were designed to provide habitat and encourage marine life, but the later Posidonia planting is a separate restoration programme. It would therefore be inaccurate to say that the six faces alone restored the seagrass meadow. Instead, the museum has become part of a broader effort to rehabilitate a damaged coastal environment.When art becomes part of the ecosystemThe Cannes experiment reflects a growing interest in combining public art with ecological restoration. Rather than building an underwater attraction and leaving the surrounding environment untouched, the project created structures intended to be gradually absorbed into the marine landscape. Research published in Science of the Total Environment reviewed restoration efforts involving Posidonia oceanica and found that active restoration can help accelerate recovery, but also stressed that the species grows slowly and that restoration methods need to be matched to local conditions. The review called for more field experiments and a better understanding of which techniques work under different environmental circumstances. That makes Cannes’ approach particularly interesting. The museum is free to visit, the sculptures sit in shallow water, and boats are prohibited from anchoring in the protected area. The result is intended to serve two purposes at once: give people an accessible way to experience marine conservation and reduce pressure on the habitat around the artworks.These six faces thus acquire an existence which goes beyond their artistic function. They started as casts of people from Cannes, but then underwent the process of becoming giant-sized sculptures that were submerged into the seabed. Now that they have been there for some time, algae, shells and other life forms have already started to grow on them, while in the meantime another restoration project is working towards returning Posidonia to the water around them. For Cannes, the biggest change that the museum will undergo might just be that which cannot be seen from the gallery floor.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Delhi Police hunts Swatantra Bharadwaj after he flees Bulandshahr on Bullet
articles.summary: NEW DELHI:  Swatantra Bharadwaj, accused of assaulting a student's father during a protest at Jantar Mantar, fled Bulandshahr hours after the Delhi Po.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Swatantra Bharadwaj, accused of assaulting a student's father during a protest at Jantar Mantar, fled Bulandshahr hours after the Delhi Police assured the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) that he would be arrested, sources told news agency PTI on Friday.According to PTI, Bharadwaj left Naithla village on a Bullet motorcycle towards Khurja and was wearing a helmet to conceal his identity.Several police teams in plain clothes were deployed to locate him. During the search, police also questioned local journalists. Efforts are underway to trace and apprehend Bharadwaj.The development follows the circulation of a video clip from an interview with Bharadwaj in which he claimed to have "cracked the skull" of Sanjay Kumar, father of student Nishu Azad, during a protest at Jantar Mantar.The CJP staged another protest in the capital on Friday at the Parliament Street police station.Party representatives said police had informed them that Bharadwaj, who boasted in an interview that he had cracked the skull of a student protester's father and got away with it, would be booked under charges of attempted murder and criminal intimidation, as well as under the SC/ST Act.They also said a separate FIR would be registered over online abuse and objectionable images targeting the assault victim's daughter."After the addition of the SC/ST Act, the victim will undergo another medical examination. Further investigation will be conducted to determine whether a charge under the attempt-to-murder section is required," a police source said.CJP co-convener Saurav Das said Delhi Police must ensure that those responsible for violence were not allowed to go unpunished."Goons like Swatantra Bharadwaj came to Jantar Mantar. Did Delhi Police not identify them? He committed attempt to murder," Das said."Delhi Police has assured action in 72 hours. If they don't fulfil the commitment, we will have to come back. We are standing with the students," he said.The protesters included Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief and MP Chandra Shekhar Azad and CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka. They accused Delhi Police of going soft on Bharadwaj.Security was stepped up around the police station, with additional personnel deployed and barricades put up.Ranka alleged that Sanjay had suffered head injuries, including a skull fracture.Delhi Police, however, disputed that Sanjay had suffered a skull fracture. Police said he sustained a minor injury during a scuffle and that a case had been registered on his complaint.Ranka alleged that Bharadwaj had openly admitted to assaulting Sanjay and attempting to kill him, but claimed that no action was taken because of the influence of BJP workers and Delhi minister Kapil Mishra.Das alleged that while protesters were holding a peaceful demonstration at Jantar Mantar, members of a criminal gang reached the site and resorted to violence."After the FIR was registered, we continued putting pressure on the police, saying that this was an attempt to murder and that the relevant section should be added," he added."We also demanded that the SC/ST Act be invoked because they (the victims) belong to a Dalit family," he said.Speaking to reporters, Nishu alleged that she faced verbal abuse and rape threats after complaining about the assault on her father and filing an FIR."I was ashamed of even stepping out. For a few weeks I could not go to school, I feel everyone is judging me. I hope police will take action," she said.What did Swatantra Bharadwaj claim?In the one-hour interview, which is available on YouTube, Bharadwaj also claimed to have political connections."I have the blessings of Hanuman upon me. And secondly, Kapil Mishra is my elder brother. They say Kapil Mishra called and I was released. Chirag Paswan is my elder brother. How many leaders do you know? Do you know Modi ji? Modi ji is also my elder brother. I have everyone's support," he said.Das called on senior BJP leaders to respond to the claims."If the goon is openly saying Kapil Mishra and Chirag Paswan made the calls and he was released, top leaders of BJP should clarify on this," he said.The CJP said it would return to the police station if Delhi Police failed to fulfil the assurances given to the delegation.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Heavy rain lashes parts of Delhi-NCR; IMD issues red alert, flights ops hit
articles.summary: DELHI: Heavy rains lashed parts of Delhi-NCR on Friday, with dark clouds engulfing the city and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a re.
articles.body: DELHI: Heavy rains lashed parts of Delhi-NCR on Friday, with dark clouds engulfing the city and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a red alert for intense rainfall, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds later in the day.The sudden downpour disrupted Janmashtami celebrations across the capital, catching many devotees off guard. Rain-soaked roads, umbrellas lining the streets and people scrambling for shelter were seen as the showers intensified.Waterlogging was reported at Indira Gandhi International Airport after heavy rainfall lashed the national capital.Heavy rainfall affected several flights arriving in Delhi, causing delays to domestic flights from Ahmedabad, Mumbai and Port Blair.IndiGo also issued a travel advisory, stating, "bad weather over Delhi had impacted flight schedules. The airline advised passengers travelling today to check their flight status on its website or app before leaving for the airport and allow additional travel time due to slower road conditions."According to the IMD’s three-hourly rainfall data, Palam recorded 3.4 mm of rainfall between 11.30 am and 2.30 pm, while Najafgarh received 0.5 mm between 8.30 am and 11.30 am. No rainfall was recorded at most other monitoring stations during the same period.In its short-range weather forecast issued at 2.15 pm, the IMD said light to moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning was likely at many places between 2.15 pm and 4.15 pm, with isolated areas expected to receive heavy rain.The weather department has also forecast another spell of light to moderate rainfall, thunderstorms and lightning across most parts of the city between 5 pm and 8 pm, with heavy rain likely at isolated locations.The IMD further said that moderate rainfall is expected at most places over the next three hours, while a few areas could receive heavy rainfall ranging from 50 mm to 100 mm. articles.title: A Las Vegas crossing guard steps in front of speeding car as it bears down on mother, 2 children; came within 10 feet
articles.summary: US News: A routine school-morning crossing turned into a frightening near-miss in Las Vegas last week when a crossing guard stepped directly into the path of a.
articles.body: A routine school-morning crossing turned into a frightening near-miss in Las Vegas last week when a crossing guard stepped directly into the path of a speeding car to protect a mother and her two children. The incident happened outside Pinecrest Academy St. Rose on Wednesday morning, with dashcam footage later capturing the moment the vehicle approached the family as they crossed the road. FOX5 Las Vegas first reported the incident, and subsequent coverage from Atlanta News First showed the family returning to thank the crossing guard, Richard Jones.Crossing guard moves between car and familyKae’la Leon Guerrero was crossing with her 5-year-old daughter, a kindergartner, while her 11-year-old son, a sixth grader, was walking behind them. The family had noticed a car approaching but initially did not realise how quickly it was travelling. As it came toward the crosswalk, Jones, who works with All City Management Services, moved into its path and positioned himself between the vehicle and the pedestrians.The car came within roughly 10 feet of the family, according to Guerrero’s account to FOX5. Earlier reporting on the incident said the vehicle ultimately stopped just short of the crosswalk. Jones later told FOX5 that he estimated the vehicle was travelling around 35 mph in a 15 mph school zone. That figure was his estimate and has not been independently confirmed. For Guerrero, the moment was a terrifying one. Her children were left shaken by what happened, and she has been trying to reassure them since.Dashcam footage captures the close callThe incident was recorded by Jake Garcia, who was driving along the road while taking his own son to another school. The footage showed just how quickly the situation unfolded and brought attention to Jones’ response. Garcia later praised the crossing guard for putting himself between the approaching vehicle and the children.Jones, however, has played down the attention surrounding his actions. He has worked as a crossing guard for four years and previously told FOX5 that he reacted instinctively when he saw the danger. The video soon circulated on social media, and people at Pinecrest Academy St. Rose began thanking Jones for his actions. School staff could be heard calling him a hero as he returned to the crossing.Family returns with a thank-youA few days after the near-miss, Guerrero and her children returned to see Jones. On Tuesday, the family surprised him with a thank-you package, an idea reportedly sparked by her young son. The gift included restaurant gift certificates, a handwritten note and a neck fan for Jones to use while working outdoors.The gesture came after Guerrero had already met Jones and watched the dashcam footage with him. The family’s relief was mixed with concern over what could have happened. Guerrero said she hopes the incident serves as a reminder to motorists to slow down in school zones and remain alert around children and crossing guards.A split-second decision that could have changed everythingThe episode has renewed attention on the risks crossing guards face while helping children and families navigate busy roads. For the Guerrero family, the difference between an ordinary school morning and a potentially devastating accident may have come down to a crossing guard seeing the danger and reacting in time.Jones may describe it as simply doing his job. But for a mother who watched a speeding car bear down on her children, the man who stepped into its path will likely be remembered as something more: the person who stood between her family and a possible tragedy.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: China is boycotting a major Asian art festival over the naming of a Taiwanese exhibition
articles.summary: A group of Chinese artists is boycotting a major art exhibition in South Korea over the organizers' plans to use the name “Taiwan Pavilion" for an exhibition...
articles.body:
SEOUL, South Korea (AP) — A group of Chinese artists is boycotting a major art exhibition in South Korea over the organizers' plans to use the name "Taiwan Pavilion" for an exhibition of works by Taiwanese artists.

China considers self-governing Taiwan to be part of its territory and rejects the island's claim to sovereignty. Beijing generally refers to Taiwan as "China's Taiwan region."

China's Foreign Ministry on Thursday criticized the South Korean organizers of the biennial Gwangju Biennale, one of Asia's most prominent art exhibitions, saying the organizers have "stubbornly clung to the wrongful practice, allowing China's Taiwan region to participate under a designation that is completely incompatible with its status."

Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said China hopes the South Korean government will uphold its political commitment to the "one China" principle through concrete action.

The Chinese artists said the same day that they were withdrawing from the festival, which opens Saturday and runs through mid-November.

The "Taiwan Pavilion" is one of about 25 small national and institutional galleries to be operated separately from the biennale's main exhibition site, under its so-called Pavilion Project.

"The organizers of the Gwangju Biennale used an incorrect name for China's Taiwan region over its participation in the exhibition, causing a political issue to spill over onto the realm of art," Chinese curator Ruan Yuelai told reporters through an interpreter. "The Chinese exhibition team cannot accept this and unanimously agreed to withdraw from the exhibition to express our strong protest."

As of Friday afternoon, the Chinese participants had not yet removed their paintings, sculptures and other works originally planned to go on display in the "China Pavilion."

The festival organizers apologize for the 'confusion'

Taiwan's Ministry of Culture said in August that Taiwan had planned to exhibit under the name "Taiwan Pavilion" but protested that organizers changed it to "National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts Pavilion."

The art festival said Wednesday that it "deeply apologizes for causing concerns and confusion" to those involved in its "Pavilion Project," and said there had been differences with the Taiwan museum over the naming issue.

Organizers said they signed a contract with the National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts over its participation, so they thought Taiwanese artists would exhibit under the museum acronym, "NTMoFA." They said the Taiwanese museum later insisted on the name "Taiwan Pavilion," and said they felt pressure to accept the name.

Earlier in the week, China also warned of consequences for Taiwan after the island's foreign minister attended a diplomatic forum in the island country of Palau. In May, China pressured an African country to exclude Taiwanese activists from an international human rights conference.

It's unclear whether the Chinese protest would trigger a major diplomatic spat with South Korea, which is now ruled by a liberal government which wants to improve ties with China, the country's biggest trading partner.

South Korea's Foreign Ministry said the naming decision was made by a non-governmental entity and has nothing to do with the government. It said South Korea hopes the latest issue won't affect relations and cooperation between the two countries.

Taiwan is a self-ruled island, but China claims it as part of its territory. The two sides split after a civil war in 1949. Beijing has stepped up its pressure on Taiwan, poaching diplomatic allies. The island now only has 12 diplomatic allies around the world.

Associated Press writer Kanis Leung in Hong Kong contributed to this report.
